newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Stronger Wall St lifts Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Stronger Wall St lifts Australian stocks at open.

text.p: Australian shares climbed at the open on Monday with Wall Street's stronger finish providing the impetus for local investors.
The All Ordinaries index added 7.6 points to 2,377.1.
The market sprinted higher from the opening bell before slowing. Banks were strongest ahead of the expected release of the Wallis report into the financial system later this week.
ANZ Bank, up one percent to A$8.10 was the pick of the big four banks.
"The better finish overseas helped although it has come back a bit from its strong start," said a Sydney-based broker.
He said the initial spurt to the day's high of 2,384.7 was always unlikely to be sustained given the way investors were viewing events in the United States.
"People are still not convinced on the Dow. It still has some way to go (down)."
The local event of note was the Wallis report, expected to be released this week, with activity in the banks underlying the market's interest in the report's contents and likely government response.

"People will be looking to see if the government releases the report in conjunction with their own statement saying they are going to implement or reject the recommendations," said a dealer at Brisbane brokerage.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about five to two, while about 42 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
